name: Studds Accessories Ltd
title: Studds Accessories Ltd - 544599 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 margin hit from styrene spike (INR135 to ~INR225 peak) is being passed through with 9% price hike, with EBITDA guided back to 14-15% in Q2 and 18-20% by Q4 FY27 if raw materials hold; utilisation 81% and 1.5m helmet capacity from October.

summary.headline: Studds Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.7% to INR169.7 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% on a styrene-driven raw material spike; management guides 14-15% in Q2.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13.7% YoY to INR169.7 crores, with two-wheeler helmet and box volume of 1.95 million units at 81% utilisation. EBITDA was INR19.6 crores (11.5% margin) and PAT INR12.3 crores (7.2% margin), hit by a sharp rise in styrene-based raw material prices (about 600 bps of margin impact) and manpower costs (about 200 bps, from a Haryana minimum wage hike). Management said effective price realisation was about 5% in Q1, with a full ~9% price increase expected from Q2 as older-price orders roll off. Growth initiatives include 1.5 million helmets of new capacity, Decathlon, an Italian subsidiary and new products.

segments.name: Domestic STUDDS (helmets)
segments.commentary: Management cited domestic EBITDA of roughly 16-17% currently, versus about 17-18% in FY26. Q1 price increases were not fully passed through in OEM, CSD/CPC and some export channels.

segments.name: SMK (premium)
segments.commentary: Export EBITDA on SMK was described as about 30-35%. SMK range is INR4,000 to INR15,000 helmets.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 21% of Q1 revenue; target is closer to 30%. Export orders executed in Q1 were contracted before the price rise; new orders are booked at revised prices.

segments.name: Bicycle helmets (Decathlon)
segments.commentary: Bicycle helmet ASPs are about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets. Commercial production expected from October 2026, with Decathlon working like an OEM relationship.

segments.name: Bluetooth and riding jackets (new)
segments.commentary: Management expects INR15-20 crores of revenue from these two categories in FY27. Some products are made in-house and some by contract manufacturers.

segments.name: Italian subsidiary
segments.commentary: Dealer-direct entry planned in Italy, Germany and France. Expected losses of about INR2-3 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28; revenue guidance EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28. Management said profits start from year 3, with 10-12% EBITDA margin cited.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 14-15%; normalised 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to stable raw material prices.
FY27 revenue growth of mid-teens guided earlier; volume growth now expected at about 10% with 7-8% blended realisation (management said high-teens revenue growth on last call).
Full ~9% price increase (on FY26 base) expected to be reflected from Q2; Q2 realisation expected at 8-9% for OEM/CSD/CPC channels.
Styrene-based raw material cost impact expected to soften to about 300 bps in Q2 from 600 bps in Q1; management expects Q3 and Q4 to improve further.
FY28 standalone guidance: volume growth 13-14% and price realisation 3-4%, implying mid-to-high teens growth (management said this excludes the Italian subsidiary).
At current styrene levels (~INR185 weighted average), PAT margin expected at about 11.5-12%, versus about 13% earlier; management expects a return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27.
Export mix rising toward 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin, per management's rough estimate.
Total capex of INR76 crores to 30 June 2026 plus INR10 crores of vendor advances; FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (INR7.5 crores spent in Q1); FY28 plan INR31 crores.

financial_highlights.change: volume growth ~8.5% YoY (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base)

qa_highlights.question: Share of styrene-based raw materials in bill of materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said styrene-based direct raw material is about 36% of consumption, with about 15% more indirect (e.g., paint); analyst confirmed 36% direct.

qa_highlights.question: Italy dealer-direct model: capturing distributor margin or absorbed by costs, and steady-state margin differential?
qa_highlights.answer: Entry planned in Italy, Germany and France where there are no strong distributors; no profit in years 1-2, with profits from year 3 at a surplus EBITDA margin of about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the 600 bps material and 200 bps other-expense margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: The 200 bps is entirely manpower cost, up after Haryana minimum wage revision effective 1 April (about 35%, unskilled from INR11,000-12,000 to INR15,000-16,000); expected to soften as 9% realisation flows in, but to persist.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9% price hike on FY26 base? Q1 vs Q2 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 9% on March 2026 base; Q1 realised about 5%, Q2 expected 8-9%, and next quarter about 9%, with CSD/CPC and some exports lagging.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume growth and realisation split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 8.5%; full-year volume closer to 10% and blended realisation 7-8%, with management referring back to high-teens revenue growth guided on last call.

qa_highlights.question: Italy subsidiary losses and revenue for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses of about INR2-2.5 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28 (corrected from earlier figures); revenue EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28, included at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 guidance of 13-14% volume and 3-4% price on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified it is standalone only, excluding the Italian subsidiary, whose ASP differs; Italy revenue is incremental on top of that.

qa_highlights.question: PAT margin outlook at current styrene levels, and export mix impact?
qa_highlights.answer: At ~INR185 styrene, PAT margin about 11.5-12% versus ~13% earlier; return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27 expected. Export mix rising to 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin.

capex_capacity: First-phase addition of 1.5 million helmets annual capacity progressing as planned, expected operational from September/October 2026; existing two-wheeler helmet and box utilisation at ~81% in Q1 FY27.
Total capex of about INR76 crores incurred up to 30 June 2026, plus INR10 crores of advances committed to vendors.
FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (described as the complete FY27 budget); about INR7.5 crores spent in Q1 FY27.
FY28 capex plan INR31 crores, which includes starting a second phase of construction (figure restated on call; analyst had cited INR28 crores).

Italian operations to be fully functional in October 2026; Decathlon commercial production from October 2026; Bluetooth mesh product first commercial production expected Q3 FY27; riding jacket commercial availability around Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 effective price realisation about 5%; full ~9% price increase on FY26 base expected to be reflected from Q2, with Q2 realisation of 8-9% in the quarter per management.
Volume growth in Q1 about 8.5% (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base); management guided FY27 volume growth closer to 10%, with blended realisation of 7-8%.

Styrene-based raw material impact about 600 bps on margin in Q1, expected to ease to about 300 bps in Q2; styrene weighted average ~INR185 currently versus ~INR225 peak and ~INR135 at start of Q4 FY26.

OEM price increases received from all customers except one, with that one expected within a week; manpower cost pass-through expected from OEMs. Management said GT channel price increase was fully passed through without resistance.

Exports about 21% of Q1 revenue, with export orders from before the price rise executed at old prices; new export orders booked at revised prices. Export SMK EBITDA about 30-35%; domestic EBITDA about 16-17% currently vs 17-18% in FY26.
Bicycle helmet (Decathlon) ASPs about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets; Bluetooth and riding jacket revenue expected at INR15-20 crores in FY27.
risks_watch: Styrene price path: management says Q2 already softening and expects Q3-Q4 better, but prices moved from ~INR135 to ~INR225 peak and are at ~INR185; Gulf supply disruption (Hormuz) is the cited driver.
Realisation lag: Q1 realised only ~5% vs ~9% target; CSD/CPC and some export channels slower to pass through; one OEM price hike still pending.
Q2 margin guidance of 14-15% and Q4 return to 18-20% depend on raw material stability; margin recovery timing could slip.
Italy and Decathlon execution: Italy start-up losses, Decathlon commercial production from October 2026, and new-product launches (Bluetooth mesh Q3 FY27, jackets Q2 FY27) all need to hit timelines.

Guidance clarity: FY28 volume/price guidance is standalone; analyst reconciliation of consolidated numbers was not fully resolved on the call, with some figures corrected during Q&A (e.g., Italy losses, EUR1 million vs INR figures).
key_quotes: The important part is what we are doing today. What is important for us is that we have not been sitting back and waiting for the commodity cycle to normalize.
So, we don't expect big losses after that.
Once our Italy operations become fully functional in October 2026, we will be much closer to the customer.
So rather than asking a distributor to forecast demand several months in advance, we can increasingly move towards a more responsive and just-in-time supply model.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and capacity, but cautious on near-term margins, with management repeatedly stressing dependence on raw material prices. Several Q&A figures were corrected on the call (Italy losses, FY28 cost, EUR revenue), which lowers confidence in the precision of the numbers.

adds.what: First-phase addition of 1.5 million helmets annual capacity

growth.why: FY27 volume growth guided at 8-10% (closer to 10%) with 7-8% blended realisation, implying roughly mid-teens revenue growth, backed by 1.5m helmet capacity from Sept/Oct 2026, a ~9% price increase from Q2, and Decathlon, Bluetooth/jacket and export initiatives, though no firm order book was quantified and utilisation is 81%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (14-15%); 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 11.5% with ~600 bps styrene hit easing to ~300 bps in Q2 and full ~9% price increase from Q2 (Q1 realisation only ~5%); management guides 14-15% in Q2 and 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to raw material stability.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: First-phase 1.5 million helmets annual capacity is under construction and progressing as planned for operation from September/October 2026, against existing utilisation of 81%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 volume grew ~8.5% (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base) and management guides FY27 volume growth of 8-10%, closer to 10%, with new capacity from Sept/Oct 2026 and FY28 standalone volume guided at 13-14%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 81% and the FY28 capex plan of INR31 crores includes starting a second phase of construction, but no new board-level capex announcement beyond the 1.5 million helmet phase was made, and FY27 capex is described as a complete INR58 crore budget.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has already cut its view from high-teens revenue growth on the last call to mid-teens for FY27 (volume ~10%, realisation 7-8%), and PAT margin at current styrene levels is now 11.5-12% versus ~13% earlier.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin guide of 14-15% and Q4 return to 18-20% depend on styrene staying around INR185 (down from ~INR225 peak), and Q1 realisation of ~5% lagged the ~9% target with CSD/CPC and some exports slower to pass through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (riding jackets) to Q3 FY27 (Bluetooth mesh); Decath
rows.why: Management expects INR15-20 crores of revenue from Bluetooth and riding jacket categories in FY27, with jackets available around Q2 FY27, Bluetooth mesh first commercial production in Q3 FY27, and Decathlon commercial production from October 2026.

rows.label: Italy dealer-direct entry (Italy, Germany, France)
rows.when: Fully functional October 2026; profits from year 3
rows.why: Italian operations to be fully functional in October 2026 with expected losses of INR2-2.5 crores in FY27 and FY28, EUR100-125k revenue in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28, and 10-12% EBITDA margin only from year 3.

rows.label: Export mix toward 30% adds 200-300 bps to PAT margin
rows.why: Exports are about 21% of Q1 revenue versus target closer to 30%, and management estimates the mix shift could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin, though it has not dated the shift.

rows.label: Remaining OEM price increase and manpower pass-through
rows.why: Price increases received from all customers except one (expected within a week), with manpower cost (about 200 bps, from ~35% minimum-wage hike) expected to be passed through by OEMs, supporting Q2 realisation of 8-9%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q4 margin recovery, 1.5m helmet capacity and the ~9% price increase, but cautious on near-term margins tied to styrene; analysts pushed on the FY28 standalone vs consolidated guidance and several Italy, EUR and FY28 figures were corrected during the Q&A.
